docs.task: How the MemoryRecall tool applies its default and maximum limits, where its description states them, and its tests.

asks: How the MemoryRecall tool applies its default and maximum limits

data_flow.step: A native agent, or a harness agent through the MCP tool memory_recall, issues MemoryRecall with optional query, area, limit. The harness name memory_recall maps to MemoryRecall through MCP_TOOLS.
The tool dispatcher routes the name to misc::memory_recall.

memory_recall reads query and area with str_arg and limit with u64_arg. A missing limit becomes DEFAULT_RECALL_LIMIT (8, from ostra-store). The value is clamped to 1..=50 by the local const MAX_RECALL_LIMIT. u64_arg accepts a JSON float and truncates it, with negative floats becoming 0 and then clamped to 1. A negative integer is not u64, and a non-number value is None, so both fall back to the default.

On spawn_blocking it opens MemoryStore and calls recall(area, query, limit). recall uses limit as the SQL LIMIT of each bucket and stops merging deduplicated lessons at limit. The store applies no maximum, so a direct caller could pass any value.
The tool formats '{n} lesson(s) recalled, most relevant first:' followed by numbered lines, or returns 'No lessons recorded for this query.' when empty.

Owns DEFAULT_RECALL_LIMIT = 8 and MemoryStore::recall, which uses limit as the per-bucket SQL LIMIT and as the cap on merged output. It does not clamp or validate limit. Its tests always pass 8.

patterns.description: MemoryRecall and DocsSearch both parse limit with u64_arg, default it, and clamp it in the tool function. Neither returns an error for an out-of-range value: 0 becomes 1, anything above the maximum becomes the maximum. The code tools do the same with MAX_LIMIT = 300 in crates/ostra-code/src/tools.rs. The JSON schema repeats the bounds as minimum and maximum, so a provider that enforces the schema rejects out-of-range values before the clamp runs.

document.problem: MemoryRecall has a default limit of 8 and a maximum of 50. The default lives in ostra-store, the maximum lives in ostra-tools, and the tool description text states only the default. The maximum appears in the JSON input schema and in docs, but not in the description prose. No test exercises the default, the clamp, or the schema bounds.

submit.findings_summary: The default of 8 is DEFAULT_RECALL_LIMIT in crates/ostra-store/src/memory.rs. The maximum of 50 is a separate const, MAX_RECALL_LIMIT, in crates/ostra-tools/src/misc.rs, where memory_recall applies `u64_arg(...).unwrap_or(DEFAULT).clamp(1, 50)`; MemoryStore::recall itself does no clamping. The MEMORY_RECALL description in crates/ostra-tools/src/defs.rs states only "limit defaults to 8." The maximum appears only in the input schema (minimum 1, maximum 50) and in docs/internals/project-memory.md and tools.md. The only test that calls MemoryRecall is memory_round_trip in misc.rs, which passes no limit. The store tests always pass 8. No test covers the default, the clamp, or the schema bounds.
